newsitem.title: USA: Paris Club - Russia deal still needs formalizing.
newsitem.headline: Paris Club - Russia deal still needs formalizing.

text.p: The Paris Club of creditor countries said the deal letting Russia join its ranks still needed formal agreement by the whole group to become final.
In a statement, the Paris Club said its chairman, Christian Noyer, had on Friday reached an understanding with Mikhail Kasyanov, Russia's vice minister of finance.
The two agreed that Russia would join "through the application of realistic broad adjustment to make Russian claims comparable with Paris Club members' claims vis-a-vis debtor countries."

"This understanding lies on a differentiation between debtors with a higher adjustment for the poorest countries, and taking account country specificities, with a view to ensure the financial sustainability of all debtors."
Russia, which inherited both the debts and the obligations of the former Soviet Union, has won a series of deals to reschedule Soviet-era debts.
It wanted to join the Paris Club as a creditor in an effort to win repayment of some debts extended to Soviet allies, most of them in the developing world.

U.S. President Bill Clinton, announcing the deal to let Russia in just before the "Summit of the Eight" began in Denver, said Russia's membership meant it would "now be a partner with the other members" in trying to promote global economic growth by relieving the debt of developing nations that adopt reforms.
"What you see here is a sweeping integration of Russia into the major decision-making networks of the world in a way that is very positive for the rest of us," Clinton said.
The "Summit of the Eight" includes the Group of Seven industrialized nations and Russia.
